key_insight: A parameterized PINN predicts 3D thermohydraulic fields across embedded microchannel designs, delivering over 10,000× lower reported computational time and cost than conventional simulation.
engineering_relevance: This physics-informed surrogate could accelerate the design and optimization of embedded liquid cooling for high-performance chips.
method: Inputs combine four geometric dimensions with three spatial coordinates.
Training combines geometric ansatz embedding, SOAP optimization, and a thermal-conductivity-based curriculum.
An optimized JAX backend enables convergence in under four hours on one consumer-grade GPU.
evidence_signal: Against finite-element simulations, the abstract reports relative errors of 8.1% for velocity fields and 5.6% for temperature fields.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the validated parameter ranges or performance outside the trained design space.
paper_title: Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Efficient Simulation of Embedded Microfluidic Chip Cooling
